lastCompletedStory.title: CRITICAL: buildConfigLogCapCommand's byte ceiling is a bash-only construct, but…

openQuestions: CAM-513 (flaky-test-isolation, filed on main from US-R1-003) remains open and unrelated to this story's diff.

US-R2-002 (viewer pane dies immediately, tail -f races the log file's own creation) and US-R2-003 (viewer freezes permanently after the first rotate, tail -f follows the unlinked pre-rotate inode) are separate, still-open, CRITICAL findings against the same v|V line/buildConfigLogCapCommand family; out of scope for this story (US-R2-001 is scoped strictly to the POSIX-sh byte-ceiling defect) but should be picked up next given their priority ordering in prd.json.

US-R2-004 (WARNING: every existing test in test/setup-config-log.test.ts spawns snippets under an explicit bash, never the real /bin/sh production tmux hands pipe-pane -o commands to, so the tmux boundary itself stays untested) is also still open; this story's new test partially narrows that gap for buildConfigLogCapCommand specifically (spawns under /bin/dash when present, falls back to /bin/sh) but does not add the real-tmux end-to-end integration test US-R2-004 asks for.
US-R2-005 (site 4 has no stale-sibling pruning, unlike sites 1/2/3/5) remains open and untouched by this story.
nextStoryContext: US-R2-001 fixed the reviewer's CRITICAL finding that buildConfigLogCapCommand's (src/commands/setup.ts) rotate guard used the bash-only `(( $(wc -c < LOG) > N ))` arithmetic-command syntax, but tmux hands a `pipe-pane -o` shell-command argument to `/bin/sh -c '...'` (tmux(1), confirmed live via Step 5.5 WebFetch against the current tmux.1 manpage: 'shell-command arguments are sh(1) commands ... Will run: /bin/sh -c ...'), and on every Linux binary this project ships (README: gateship-linux-x64/arm64) /bin/sh is dash, which does not recognize `(( ))` as a construct and mis-parses it as nested subshells. Verified by hand under real /bin/dash before writing any fix: the pre-fix snippet fed 3000 bytes against a 500-byte ceiling produced `dash: N: 3000: not found`, left the log at the full unbounded 3000 bytes (cap never fired), AND created a stray file literally named `500` in the writer's cwd (the user's repository, since lsof confirms the pipe-pane job's cwd is the repo, tripping the plan-preflight clean-tree guard, ADR-0014). macOS's own /bin/sh (bash 3.2 posix mode) tolerates `(( ))`, which is why this only ever reproduced on Linux and nothing on macOS CI noticed. IMPORTANT DEVIATION FROM THE STORY'S OWN SUGGESTED FIX: the story description proposed `test "$(wc -c < LOG)" -gt N` (quoted) verbatim, but that form is unsafe for this specific call site: the snippet's returned text is embedded verbatim inside the OUTER menu script's own double-quoted `"tmux pipe-pane ... -o '...'"` argument to split-window (buildSetupMenuScript, the same three-level quoting trace the pre-existing US-R1-004 patterns.md bullet documents), so any literal `"` in the returned string closes that outer double-quoted argument early and corrupts the generated .cam-setup-menu.sh script -- confirmed empirically by generating the real buildSetupMenuScript() output with the quoted form applied and observing the stray `"` mid-string, then re-confirming with `bash -n` only after removing it. The actual fix instead uses `test $(wc -c < LOG) -gt N`, UNQUOTED: still POSIX-correct (word-splitting the unquoted `$(wc -c < LOG)` on IFS whitespace is safe here because `wc -c`'s output, even BSD/macOS's whitespace-padded form, is always exactly one numeric token with nothing else to collide with) and reintroduces zero quote characters, matching the pre-existing zero-quote convention this whole snippet family (buildConfigLogCapCommand/buildConfigLogCleanupCommand's embedding) already relies on. The updated regression test (test/setup-config-log.test.ts, new 'runs correctly under a real POSIX-strict sh' case) asserts three things: (1) the returned command string contains neither `((` nor any `"`/`'` character (a structural guard that would have caught the naive quoted-fix regression before ever spawning a shell), (2) spawning the real command under /bin/dash if present (else /bin/sh, this dev machine and macOS 26 runner images both have /bin/dash at /bin/dash; falls back gracefully, no it.skip used so the skip-ratchet/version-skip gates are untouched) with 6x the ceiling of input caps the resulting file at or under the ceiling, and (3) no stray ceiling-named file is left in the writer's cwd. All 12 tests in that file pass (up from 11), full bun test 6100 pass / 0 fail (+1 from the new test), typecheck 0 errors, full bun run check:all spine green after two file-size-budget.json raises for src/commands/setup.ts (1017->1032 for the fix + doc comment, then ->1044 once the doc comment explaining the zero-quote deviation was added; both under one dated US-R2-001/CAM-510 _ref note, minimal 2-line-changed diff via targeted line patch rather than a full JSON reserialize). No vendor/templates changes, no embed-vendor needed. Step 5.5 fetched the current tmux.1 manpage from the tmux GitHub master branch, confirming the /bin/sh -c invocation claim the story and this fix both depend on. scripts/cam/prd.json was already modified on disk at session start (US-R2-002 through at least US-R2-006 already present with passes:false, pre-existing supervisor-owned state, not written by this session) and was deliberately left untouched/uncommitted by this story, per the AGENT.md rule that the implementer never edits prd.json.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Confirmed tmux's own manpage states shell-command arguments (which pipe-pane -o's value is) are sh(1) commands run as '/bin/sh -c ...', matching the story's claim and the reason buildConfigLogCapCommand's rotate guard must stay POSIX-sh-safe rather than bash-only.
